log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Floette used Light of Ruin → Clefable
Floette used Light of Ruin → Clefable

decisions.rationale: Pelipper leads to set Drizzle, powering Surf and weakening Fire moves. Gengar follows to Mega Evolve immediately, gaining Shadow Tag to trap one foe for a 2v1 advantage. Garchomp in back safely sets Stealth Rock behind Focus Sash and threatens physical coverage. Clefable provides Wish/Protect/Light Screen support and walls Mega Floette's special assault with Magic Guard and massive SpD.
decisions.notebook: Rain team plan: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag eliminates one non-Ghost foe outright. Pelipper Drizzle enables spread Surf damage and weakens opposing Fire (hurts Talonflame). Tailwind from Pelipper lets Meowscarada outrun everything late-game. Garchomp is Electric-immune, sets Stealth Rock, breaks physical walls. Clefable walls special attackers, provides Wish+LightScreen. Toxapex and Meowscarada are flexible bench options — Toxapex for physical walling/Toxic Spikes, Meowscarada as Protean cleaner with Flower Trick/Sucker Punch/Brick Break.

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Manectric plus Sneasler gives immediate Fake Out control against Mega Gengar and strong Pelipper pressure. Floette is preserved to punish Garchomp and Toxapex, while Talonflame provides emergency Tailwind and burn support versus their physical attackers.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: lead Manectric + Sneasler for Fake Out control into possible Mega Gengar and Thunderbolt pressure into Pelipper. Keep Floette healthy for Garchomp/Toxapex pressure; Talonflame is the speed-control and physical-check reserve. Avoid bringing Palafin into an early Mega Gengar Shadow Tag position unless its pivot is already unnecessary.

decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar gets Shadow Tag, trapping both non-Ghost foes. Shadow Ball on Sneasler is 2x super effective. Pelipper Tailwind gives +1 Speed to allies for 4 turns, enabling faster switches and outspeeding threats.
decisions.notebook: Rain team plan: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag eliminates non-Ghost foes. Pelipper Drizzle active. Tailwind set for speed control. Garchomp and Clefable remain as clean/utility options. Prioritize trapping and weakening the Sneasler-Manectric core.

decisions.rationale: Switch Garchomp for Pelipper: Ground typing gives Electric immunity vs Manectric-Mega, and Shadow Tag traps both active foes. Sneasler's Protect was used last turn, so Garchomp's speed advantage lets it threaten with Earthquake. Gengar-Mega passes to maintain trap pressure.
decisions.notebook: Rain team plan: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost foes. Pelipper fainted turn 1 to Manectric Thunderbolt. Opponent Manectric-Mega and Sneasler are both trapped. Need to manage Sneasler's Life Orb Gunk Shot and Manectric's Overheat/Snarl. Garchomp and Clefable remain as clean/utility options. Prioritize weakening the Sneasler-Manectric core while preserving bulk.

decisions.rationale: Mega Manectric’s Thunderbolt is a guaranteed OHKO on Damp Rock Pelipper. Protect preserves Life Orb Sneasler from Gengar’s possible attack while denying unnecessary chip; Fake Out into Pelipper adds no value once Thunderbolt removes it.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent revealed Pelipper (Damp Rock, Drizzle; Hurricane/Surf/Roost/Tailwind) and Gengar (Gengarite, Cursed Body; Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt). Pelipper is always OHKOed by Manectric Thunderbolt. Gengar can Mega Evolve for Shadow Tag and may outspeed un-Mega Manectric depending on investment; its Shadow Ball does not OHKO full regular Manectric. Preserve Floette for Garchomp/Toxapex pressure and Talonflame for Tailwind/physical control.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake hits both trapped foes for 2x super-effective spread damage, maximizing pressure. Shadow Ball on Sneasler adds safe 100%-accurate damage to the faster physical threat. Both foes are Shadow-Tagged and cannot switch, so chip damage accumulates. Acceptable that Gengar-Mega takes neutral spread recoil.
decisions.notebook: Rain team plan active. Pelipper fainted to Manectric Thunderbolt. Manectric-Mega and Sneasler are both Shadow-Tagged by Mega Gengar and cannot switch. Garchomp and Clefable remain as clean/utility options. Prioritize weakening the Sneasler-Manectric core while preserving bulk. Sneasler Protect success reduced next use.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Protect preserves Manectric from Garchomp's potentially lethal Earthquake while Sneasler gets guaranteed Close Combat damage into Garchomp. Sneasler is likely targeted down, but retaining full Manectric plus both backline options is preferable to exposing both actives to Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent revealed Pelipper: Damp Rock, Drizzle, Hurricane/Surf/Roost/Tailwind; Manectric Thunderbolt OHKOs it. Mega Gengar is Timid with Shadow Tag and Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt; Mega Manectric is faster and Gengar Shadow Ball is substantial but not a full-HP OHKO on Manectric. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash with Rough Skin and Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Preserve Floette for Garchomp/Toxapex pressure and Talonflame for Tailwind/physical control. Garchomp Earthquake can potentially OHKO Manectric and does 50-73% to Sneasler as spread damage; Sneasler Close Combat only does roughly 26-45% to Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Bring Floette-Eternal: it can immediately threaten the weakened Garchomp with Moonblast while retaining strong endgame pressure against the possible Toxapex or Meowscarada.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 revealed Pelipper: Damp Rock, Drizzle, Hurricane/Surf/Roost/Tailwind; Mega Manectric Thunderbolt OHKOs it. Mega Gengar is Timid with Shadow Tag and Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt; Mega Manectric outspeeds it. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash with Rough Skin and Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Preserve Floette for Dragon/Ground and possible Toxapex pressure; Talonflame supplies Tailwind, Focus Sash utility, and physical disruption. Opponent's fourth is one of Clefable, Toxapex, or Meowscarada.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Garchomp)
decisions.rationale: Earthquake spreads heavy damage: 2x on Manectric-Mega (Ground vs Electric in Rain) threatens a KO, 1x on Floette-Eternal, and some recoil on Clefable is acceptable. Light Screen halves Floette-Eternal's super-effective Fairy special attacks, which are the biggest remaining threat to both of your Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Rain active. Shadow Tag from Mega Gengar locks Manectric-Mega and Sneasler (fainted). Gengar and Pelipper out. Garchomp low HP but can trade damage. Manectric-Mega Intimidate revealed. Prioritize breaking the Manectric-Floette core. Light Screen mitigates Fairy STAB threat from Floette-Eternal next turn. Preserve Clefable as the special wall.

decisions.rationale: Overheat acts before Garchomp and has a strong chance to remove it before Earthquake; Moonblast is the accurate backup KO and is immune to Dragon Claw. This minimizes the chance Manectric is lost while guaranteeing Garchomp falls even if Overheat misses or falls short.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Clefable is Calm, Magic Guard, Light Clay, with Moonblast/Wish/Protect/Light Screen. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash Rough Skin with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Mega Manectric is faster than Garchomp and Mega Gengar; Floette is immune to Garchomp Dragon Claw and threatens it with Fairy STAB. Rain from Damp Rock Pelipper is active when Pelipper leads.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is fainted so must pass. Clefable should Moonblast Manectric-Mega for neutral damage to break the opponent's core; Manectric is already at -2 SpA and weakened, making it the vulnerable target. Hitting Floette-Eternal with Moonblast would be resisted (Fairy vs Fairy 0.5x).
decisions.notebook: Rain active. Shadow Tag from Mega Gengar locks Manectric-Mega and Sneasler (fainted). Gengar and Pelipper out. Manectric-Mega Intimidate revealed. Light Screen active on my side. Prioritize breaking the Manectric-Floette core. Clefable is key special wall—preserve it. Opponent's Manectric is at -2 SpA, making it less threatening; Floette-Eternal remains the bigger offensive threat next turn.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Clefable: Light of Ruin is Floette’s strongest available damage through Light Screen, while Mega Manectric adds damage before Clefable can act. This gives the best immediate KO chance and prevents Wish from extending the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 confirmed: Pelipper is Bold Damp Rock Drizzle with Hurricane/Surf/Roost/Tailwind. Mega Gengar is Timid Gengarite with Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt. Clefable is Calm Magic Guard Light Clay with Moonblast/Wish/Protect/Light Screen. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash Rough Skin with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Mega Manectric outspeeds Garchomp and Mega Gengar; Floette is immune to Garchomp Dragon Claw and threatens it with Fairy STAB.

decisions.rationale: Wish is the only move that improves Clefable's HP from 24% toward ~50-68% after heal, which is essential since Moonblast cannot KO Floette-Eternal (78%) in one hit and Manectric is already neutralized by Shadow Tag at -3 SpA. Moonblast on either foe leaves Clefable too low to survive the double hit. Preserving HP maximizes the chance of outlasting and grinding down both opponents over subsequent turns.
decisions.notebook: Rain 4 turns left. Light Screen 6 turns on my side. Shadow Tag from Mega Gengar permanently locks Manectric-Mega (55% HP, -3 SpA) and Sneasler (fainted). Floette-Eternal (78%) is the primary offensive threat. Opponent's 4th slot is one unknown of Talonflame/Archaludon/Palafin. Garchomp fainted with Stealth Rock (PP 20/20) and 3 other moves available. Clefable is my last Pokémon—preserve it as the special wall. Plan: use Wish to recover HP, then Moonblast Manectric to remove the locked threat, then focus Floette-Eternal.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt adds guaranteed chip before Floette’s Light of Ruin, which is a guaranteed KO through Light Screen from Clefable’s shown HP. This maximizes the chance to close immediately while retaining a fallback if Light of Ruin misses.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 confirmed: Pelipper is Bold Damp Rock Drizzle with Hurricane/Surf/Roost/Tailwind. Mega Gengar is Timid Gengarite with Shadow Ball/Sludge Wave/Focus Blast/Thunderbolt. Clefable is Calm Magic Guard Light Clay with Moonblast/Wish/Protect/Light Screen. Garchomp is Jolly Focus Sash Rough Skin with Earthquake/Stone Edge/Dragon Claw/Stealth Rock. Mega Manectric outspeeds Garchomp and Mega Gengar; Floette is immune to Garchomp Dragon Claw and threatens it with Fairy STAB. Under Light Screen, Floette Light of Ruin is materially stronger than Moonblast and can secure KOs Moonblast may miss.

reflections.summary: Loss stems primarily from a flawed team-preview plan: bringing Pelipper (rain setter) handed the opponent's Manectric-Mega perfect-accuracy Thunders and a speed-summoning environment that favored them. Gengar-Mega's Shadow Tag trapped Manectric but Gengar was too frail to capitalize before fainting to Sneasler's Close Combat. Garchomp never got to use Stealth Rock. Clefable, left as the last Pokémon, could not sustain the combined pressure of Manectric's Thunderbolt and Floette-Eternal's Light of Ruin even behind Light Screen. We had no super-effective answer for Floette-Eternal and no meaningful hazard pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, do not bring rain support against this opponent — Manectric-Mega thrives in rain. Instead, lead with or reserve a Pokémon carrying strong Poison- or Steel-type coverage (e.g., Garchomp with Poison Jab or a dedicated Poison type) to threaten Floette-Eternal, and ensure Stealth Rock is actually set before the midgame pressure peaks. Prioritize a revenge-killer or faster pivot that can dent or remove Manectric after Gengar's lock expires.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Manectric-Mega (Intimidate, Thunder/Overheat/Snarl) + Floette-Eternal (Pixilate Light of Ruin 140 BP, Moonblast) — both extremely dangerous in rain. Sneasler is Jolly/Life Orb/PoisonTouch, runs Close Combat as main STAB. Opponent's 4th slot still unresolved (Talonflame/Archaludon/Palafin) — must scout next game. Shadow Tag successfully locked Manectric but insufficient offensive follow-through. Light Screen + Wish on Clefable inadequate vs. double-target pressure. Avoid rain support next game; prioritize hazard setup, Poison/Steel coverage for Floette, and revenge-kill speed control.

reflections.summary: Won because Mega Manectric + Sneasler was the right anti-rain lead: Manectric immediately removed Pelipper, while Sneasler traded for Mega Gengar and left Garchomp in clean-up range. Floette then matched well into the revealed Garchomp/Clefable backline. The four brought and Mega Manectric evolution suited this opponent.
reflections.adjustment: In game 2, strongly consider repeating Mega Manectric + Sneasler into a likely Pelipper/Gengar lead, but prioritize preserving Sneasler if Gengar can be removed without the trade; keep Floette ready for Garchomp and use Light of Ruin through Clefable's Light Screen when a KO matters.
reflections.notebook: G1 revealed opponent's chosen structure was Pelipper + Mega Gengar lead with Garchomp + Clefable in back; Clefable set Light Screen once brought in. Their rain lead is highly vulnerable to Mega Manectric Thunderbolt, and Mega Manectric + Sneasler successfully pressures both Pelipper and Mega Gengar. Floette is a strong planned backline answer to Garchomp/Clefable, including through Light Screen with Light of Ruin.
